basic_identification.sector_category: Mechanical Engineering / Photographic and Cinematographic Equipment (finalized by the Photographic and Cinematographic Equipment Sectional Committee, MED 32, under the Mechanical Engineering Division Council of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Photographic and Cinematographic Equipment Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This Indian Standard specifies the recorded characteristic for magnetic sound records on 16 mm full-coat perforated magnetic film and 16 mm motion-picture film with magnetic striping when used at the nominal speed of 24 frames [18.3 cm (7.2 in)] per second or 25 frames [19.05 cm (7.5 in)] per second, to guarantee seamless post-production audio exchange.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Product Specification. Manufacturers of magnetic films and post-production studios are highly encouraged to conform to the standards of IS 11932 to receive national certification and to ensure seamless exchange of audio masters with domestic and international networks (including Doordarshan and All India Radio).

requirements.detail: The nominal recorded characteristics apply when the 16 mm magnetic film is operated at a projection frame rate of 24 frames per second, which corresponds to a linear film velocity of 18.3 cm/s (7.2 in/s).
Alternatively, the nominal recorded characteristics apply at a television-compatible frame rate of 25 frames per second, which corresponds to a linear film velocity of 19.05 cm/s (7.5 in/s).

With constant sine-wave input, the nominal short-circuit magnetic flux versus frequency curve must fall in conformity with the electrical impedance of a parallel RC combination having a time constant of exactly 70 microseconds (70 µs).

The nominal response level (N, in decibels) must comply with the logarithmic equation: N = -10 * log10(1 + 4 * pi^2 * f^2 * t^2), where f is the frequency in hertz and t is the time constant of 70 microseconds.
For recorded frequencies from 40 Hz up to 1000 Hz (1 kHz), the short-circuit magnetic flux on the film must fall within a tight tolerance of ±1.0 dB relative to the nominal curve.
For recorded frequencies from 1000 Hz up to 8000 Hz (8 kHz), the short-circuit magnetic flux on the film must fall within a tolerance of ±1.5 dB relative to the nominal curve.
For recorded frequencies from 8000 Hz up to 12500 Hz (12.5 kHz), the short-circuit magnetic flux on the film must fall within a tolerance of ±2.0 dB relative to the nominal curve.
For recorded frequencies from 12500 Hz up to 16000 Hz (16 kHz), the short-circuit magnetic flux on the film must fall within a tolerance of ±3.0 dB relative to the nominal curve.

All evaluated and reported physical parameters, frequencies, and decibel ratios must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 11932 : 1986 (Reaffirmed 2021) is the primary national Indian Standard code of practice prescribing the recorded characteristics, frequency curves, and nominal speed requirements for full-coat 16 mm magnetic sound recording on celluloid films. Maintained under the Photographic and Cinematographic Equipment Sectional Committee (MED 32) and identical to ISO 1188:1984, the code unifies movie sound recording in India. It defines a nominal frequency-response curve based on a parallel RC circuit with a 70 microsecond (70 µs) time constant, specifies linear velocities for standard projection speeds of 24 frames/sec (18.3 cm/s) and 25 frames/sec (19.05 cm/s), establishes strict decibel tolerances (ranging from ±1.0 dB to ±3.0 dB) across the audible spectrum (40 Hz to 16 kHz), and coordinates with mechanical, dimensional, and OHS safety standards to ensure robust audio engineering in post-production studios.
